Title: Bersatu calls out PN and Pas, saying 'don't play the victim'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has hit back at Perikatan Nasional and Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, saying "cowards" better describes PN leaders who avoid facing member parties.
Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said PN leaders should not "play the victim".
He said the term "cowards" could also be applied to those who abused administrative power and breached the PN constitution to deny Bersatu the right to attend the PN seat consultation committee meeting and the PN supreme council's extraordinary meeting.
"Do not talk about courage if the PN chairman (Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar) and leaders do not dare to face their own member party. That is the real cowardice," he said in a statement.
Tun Faisal was responding to Takiyuddin, who earlier today in a press conference at the Dewan Rakyat called Bersatu "cowards" who "throw stones and hide their hands".
Takiyuddin, who is also Kota Baru member of parliament, claimed Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had spoken in the media of about eight complaints to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) but had not told PN what they were.
Tun Faisal said Takiyuddin had himself acknowledged being summoned by the RoS to explain the complaints.
"After giving evidence for four hours, it is impossible that he does not know what complaints Bersatu submitted to the RoS, unless he did not pay attention to what the RoS raised or does not understand what he answered," he said.
He said the complaints arose because Pas, as leader of PN, had repeatedly breached the PN constitution, abused power, bypassed PN, failed to carry out supreme council decisions, vetoed them, and oppressed Bersatu and denied its rights as a member.
Tun Faisal said RoS was the authority over registered societies, adding that Bersatu had also made its complaints public.
He said Bersatu had repeatedly pointed out breaches of the PN constitution and supreme council decisions by Pas.
Tun Faisal urged Takiyuddin to "stop playing the victim" and answer the issues with facts and law.
"There is no need for spin. Deny Bersatu's complaints one by one, as raised by the RoS to Takiyuddin, with evidence," he said.
He said Takiyuddin should only have to answer a simple question of whether Bersatu's complaints were true.
"If Pas did not breach the PN constitution, simply submit the explanation, meeting minutes, correspondence and relevant documents to deny each allegation. It is not difficult," he said.
On Sept 22, the
RoS issued a notice
under Section 13(2) of the Societies Act 1966, giving PN 30 days to explain why its registration should not be cancelled. On Sept 23, the RoS issued a follow-up order under Section 13(2A), officially suspending all of PN's activities.
PN filed a
judicial review application
on Monday at the High Court to quash the two notices.

Title: More than 200 attend funeral of Gerik crash victim
Article:
BACHOK: More than 200 family members, villagers and friends attended the funeral of one of the victims of a three-vehicle crash in Gerik, Perak, tonight.
Mohamad Hafiz Daniel Nik Hairey, 19, was buried at 10.45pm at the Kampung Tok Jawa Islamic Cemetery in Budi here.
Earlier, funeral prayers were held at his family home before villagers and friends carried his body on foot for about 200 metres to the cemetery.
His father, Nik Hairey Nik Rahim, 42, said the last time he saw his son was on Saturday night, before Hafiz left for Gerik at 4am on Sunday.
He said Hafiz had told his mother that he had work in Perak and planned to travel there with a friend, but did not elaborate on the nature of the work.
"That afternoon, we received news of his death at about 6pm," he said when met at the Kampung Tok Jawa Islamic Cemetery in Budi, Tawang, here tonight.
Nik Hairey said his son had shown no signs that he was about to leave the family for good.
He described Hafiz as a cheerful person with many friends, evident from the large turnout at his funeral.
Hafiz, who worked selling nasi ayam gepuk at night markets, was earlier accorded funeral prayers at Taiping Hospital, Perak, before his body arrived at his family home in Kampung Tok Jawa at 7pm today.
He was the eldest of four siblings, aged 15, 10 and four, to Nik Hairey and his wife Norazira Mohd Nasir, 41.
It was reported earlier that four people, including a woman and a three-year-old girl, were killed in the crash involving a Perodua Axia, Proton Persona and lorry at Kilometre 38.5 of the East-West Highway (JRTB) Gerik-Jeli in Perak at about 12.50pm on Sunday.
The victims were Mohamad Hafiz Daniel, his friend Al Zubair Deraman, 31, and Tuan Syazrin Tuan Mud, 40, and his daughter, Safiyya Haura Mohamad Sanuzi, three.
Another of Tuan Syazrin's children, Mohamad Shiraz Hammani Abdul Fattah, nine, was seriously injured.

Title: Thai youths carry on fight for right to dissent
Article:
FIFTY years after a student demonstration against dictatorship ended in a massacre, Thailand's latest generation of protesters say they still face threats. Nutthanit Duangmusit, 24, spent several months in pre-trial detention before being convicted under Thailand's strict royal defamation law, among almost 300 people charged under so-called lese majeste since 2020. She is on bail while she appeals against her conviction and has been helping organise commemorations for today's anniversary of the Oct 6, 1976 killings at Thammasat University.
In one of the darkest chapters in modern Thai history, security forces and right-wing mobs massacred student protesters at one of the nation's top universities. "Back then, guns were fired and bodies lay on the ground," Nutthanit said as she walked AFP through the campus in Bangkok. "Today, the violence comes through the law."
The crackdown followed the return of military dictator Thanom Kittikachorn, who was ousted three years earlier. Students gathered at Thammasat to oppose his return. At dawn on Oct 6, police and right-wing groups stormed the campus, shooting, beating and lynching protesters.
The official death toll was 46, but survivors and witnesses believe more than 100 were killed. Government spokesman Ekkapob Pianpises said many of those involved in the incident have since died or could not be located.
The incident receives scant attention in Thai textbooks, leaving younger generations to learn about it from survivors and independent research. Nutthanit and her friends draw a clear line from 1976 to today, where the military is no longer in charge but conservative forces still wield significant influence.
She was involved in youth-led protests that began in 2020, which drew tens of thousands to demand democratic change and reform of the monarchy. In 2022, Nutthanit, then 20, and others polled Bangkok passersby about royal motorcades and the exercise of royal power. That and other political activities led to three convictions under lese majeste.
When many young protesters ended up in court, they were helped by lawyers, including Thammasat survivor Krisadang Nutcharut. Ahead of the anniversary, he expressed admiration for their courage and said a lese majeste reform was something "no one dares raise in my generation".
The protest movement has since subsided, with many activists imprisoned or fleeing abroad. The monarchy remains widely revered in Thailand, a largely traditionalist society where a conservative government was elected this year.
The memory of the massacre still triggers strong emotions on the other side. Chalermchai Majchaklam, now 73, was a vocational student at a rival institution who fought against the protesters. He accused the Thammasat students of attacking police and others from his institution, and said he believed they were trying to overthrow the monarchy. "We were there because we love the monarchy and we were angry," he said, adding that he would do it again.
Thiraphop Tengprawat, 21, was charged with lese majeste over a satirical banner displayed on another Thammasat campus last October after the university cancelled student events following the death of Queen Sirikit, the current king's mother. Police alleged the banner insulted Sirikit. "The problems we face today have a history," said Thiraphop, who is still waiting to hear if he will face trial.
The military seized power on the evening of the massacre and increased the punishment for royal defamation 15 days later. "The version of lese majeste enforced today is a legacy of that coup," said reform campaigner Nasree Phumkuea, 23.
Recent attempts to amend the lese majeste law have landed dozens of former and current members of parliament in court. For Nutthanit, the battle is increasingly personal. In May 2024, her close friend Netiporn Sanesangkhom died in custody following a prolonged hunger strike. She was 28.
"Fifty years later, people are still dying for justice or being forced into exile," Nutthanit said. "It feels as though Thailand keeps returning to the same place."
The writer is from AFP

Title: Repatriation of Myanmar detainees carried out in orderly, responsible and lawful manner - Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Any action regarding the repatriation of Myanmar detainees to their home country will be carried out in an orderly, responsible, and lawful manner, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the matter was among matters discussed during his meeting with the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) today to exchange views and obtain feedback regarding detainee management issues.
"Among the matters discussed included the repatriation of Myanmar refugees to their home country, including implementation procedures and security aspects, in addition to humanitarian matters that Suhakam requested be given attention.
"Meetings like this are important to enable the government to listen to the views of all parties, especially from a humanitarian perspective in handling refugee issues," he said via a Facebook post today.
Fahmi also thanked Suhakam Chairman Datuk Seri Mohd Hishamudin Mohd Yunus and his team for their willingness to receive him and his delegation during the meeting.
On Sept 29, Malaysia began the first phase of the repatriation programme for approximately 1,500 Myanmar nationals, which is part of the 5,000 individuals whom the government stated had agreed to return voluntarily from detention centers.
The government takes note of public concerns regarding foreign national management, including aspects of security, public order, and immigration detention, with every action carried out in accordance with the law and established procedures.

Title: Trump won't be a quiet lame duck after midterm polls
Article:
WHAT'S more volatile than President Donald Trump? The answer may be a lame duck Donald Trump after the United States midterm elections. The 80-year-old billionaire faces a bruising final two years in the White House if Republicans lose control of Congress in the Nov 3 polls amid voter anger over the Iran war and soaring prices. Investigations and a possible third impeachment would loom as his Democratic foes seek revenge. The president who loves to boast of his power would find much of it stymied.
But Trump with his back to the wall could cause major upheaval, from revenge at home to wars abroad — and influencing the race to be his successor in 2028. "I don't think he is going to go out with a whimper, he's going to try to go out with a bang," said Allan Lichtman, a professor at American University and author of Great American Presidents: The Twelve Who Transformed the Nation. "He can't stand not being the centre of attention. So this may spark him to be even more aggressive."
US presidents are often punished in midterm elections, weakening their party in Congress and leaving them with the dreaded lame duck epithet as their power wanes towards the end.
But if Republicans lose the House of Representatives as expected —and possibly the Senate too —Trump will find himself in a precarious position as Democrats probe alleged corruption or abuse of power. He has already signalled he will take his usual combative approach. "They'll probably go after me, and I'll go after them," Trump said in a Time Magazine interview published this week. "I think he's going to be in attack mode," said Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution.
First of all, Trump baselessly disputed his 2020 presidential election loss to Joe Biden and it is "entirely possible" he could claim irregularities in the midterms as well, said Hass. Then, Trump could direct the Department of Justice to investigate leading Democrats probing him, in the same way that a number of his opponents have found themselves facing legal action.
In the longer term, Trump sometimes hints at running for a constitutionally-barred third term in the White House, even wearing a "Trump 2028" hat at a gala media dinner in July. Lichtman said talk of a third term was to "stay relevant", but added that Trump would "keep the focus on himself by being the kingmaker" for the Republican nomination.
Trump —who hosted the television show The Apprentice in which he uttered the catchphrase "you're fired" — has been coy about backing either Vice-President JD Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio for the top job. "I assume he'll want to keep the suspense," said Hass. "Who's going to watch the show if it's already been predetermined who's the winner?"
Outgoing US presidents have often doubled down on foreign policy in the waning days of their terms, as it's the area in which they have the most power. Trump said he may resume bombing Iran after the midterms, but prolonging a quagmire that his MAGA base hates could be politically and militarily risky. "You could make the argument that he'll let it rip, but I don't think he wants his legacy to be a warmonger. "He wants his legacy to have left America stronger," said Hass, who served in the National Security Council under president Barack Obama.
Hass expected Trump to continue the US pullback from some of its western allies while maintaining detente with authoritarian Russia and China and keeping a focus on Latin America. On trade, however, Trump would likely remain "unrelentingly active", as shown by his recent hostility towards Canada, Hass said.
Trump, like many other soon-to-be retirees, ultimately may be more interested in a little home improvement. The real estate tycoon appears increasingly obsessed by his construction projects at the White House, such as his new ballroom and helipad. For Trump, stamping his mark on Washington in granite and concrete may be the greatest legacy of all.
"I love doing it," Trump said during a recent event at the White House, "because that's what I did my whole life."
The writer is from AFP

Title: New legal certification course expected to begin by 2029 latest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The New Bar Course (NBC), which will replace the Certificate in Legal Practice (CLP) examination, is expected to be implemented in 2028, or, at the latest by 2029.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Sri Azalina Othman Said said the Legal Profession Qualifying Board had established a task force on April 27 to develop the operational framework for the new course.
"Currently, the board, together with the NBC task force, is taking the necessary steps to implement the course," she said in a written parliamentary reply.
She was responding to a question from S. Kesavan (PH-Sungai Siput) on the latest status of the NBC's implementation and when the course would be introduced.
Azalina said preparations include developing course content and question banks for the Conversion Course (CC) and Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate (LPPC), as well as procuring learning management and computer-based assessment systems.
She said the board is also preparing academic regulations for the CC and LPPC and strengthening its organisational structure and workforce to operate both programmes.
She added that preparations also included developing the capacity of question setters, examiners and assessors, as well as setting criteria for course providers to conduct the LPPC.
"Based on the preparations required and policies that need to be formulated by the board, the NBC is expected to be implemented in 2028 or, at the latest, 2029," she said.

Title: PTPTN loan arrears hit RM10.7bil involving 1.16mil borrowers
Article:
PTPTN loan arrears hit RM10.7bil involving 1.16mil borrowers
Amalia Azmi, Hakim Mahari
KUALA LUMPUR: National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan arrears involving 1.16 million borrowers have reached RM10.7 billion as of Aug 31.
The Higher Education Ministry said PTPTN was taking various measures to ensure the long-term sustainability of its financing model, including strengthening loan management and improving repayment collection.
It said loan terms and conditions would be refined to better target financing to those in need, based on PTPTN's financial capacity.
"PTPTN will also improve the effectiveness and efficiency of loan repayment collection through enforcement measures and strategic cooperation with government agencies and corporations," it said in a written parliamentary reply today.
The ministry was responding to Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias (BN-Jelebu) regarding the latest amount owed by PTPTN borrowers and measures being taken to improve loan repayments.
It said, however, it remained mindful of borrowers who were genuinely struggling to repay their loans.
It said such borrowers were encouraged to come forward for consultation and restructure their repayments according to their financial capacity, or apply for a repayment deferment subject to the flexibility allowed by PTPTN.

Title: Nearly 10,000 development projects worth RM944bil proposed for 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Economy Ministry has received 9,955 new and ongoing development project proposals costing RM944 billion for 2027.
The ministry said a RM80.4 billion development ceiling would be required for consideration under the 2027 development planning process.
"Under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) 2026-2030, ministries and agencies may submit applications for proposed development programmes and projects for consideration by the Economy Ministry through the rolling plan process," it said in a written parliamentary reply today.
The ministry was responding to Datuk Seri Doris Sophia Brodi (GPS-Sri Aman) on the mechanism used by the government to ensure every announcement of development projects is accompanied by clear allocations, implementation timelines, targets and responsible agencies.
The ministry said engagement sessions were also held with other ministries, state governments and relevant agencies to ensure project priorities were based on needs, implementation capacity and established timelines.
"This is to ensure that approved projects can be implemented in an orderly manner, fully utilised within the current year and completed according to schedule for the wellbeing of the people, state development and local communities," it said.
The ministry said 13MP had also set a target of having no development projects pending commencement in the second year after approval, with the target set at zero per cent by 2030.
It said the measure was aimed at ensuring approved projects could be implemented promptly.

Title: NST Leader: Schools need stronger safeguards against violence
Article:
It is ironic that while schools and hostels are meant to protect students, some of the gravest dangers can come from within.
Last month, a 14-year-old boy died after being found unconscious at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, with police investigating an alleged assault. On Saturday, a 16-year-old schoolgirl was found dead in a school hall in Yong Peng, and three male schoolmates have been detained in connection with her death.
These tragedies are a grim reminder that schools and hostels, which should be safe places for children, are not immune to violence. Between 2021 and 2026, Malaysia has seen a disturbing series of bullying and assault cases involving students.
The Education Ministry's Student Discipline System recorded 21,307 bullying cases between 2021 and 2025.
The numbers alone are cause for concern. But repeated cases of violence raise a more fundamental question: are existing safeguards enough to protect students from threats within the school community? This is not to suggest that every incident has the same cause.
Bullying, hazing, peer violence and failures of supervision can have different causes. What they have in common is the potential to escalate when warning signs are missed, complaints are ignored or supervision fails.
In boarding schools, an entrenched culture of seniority can foster intimidation, hazing and peer-enforced punishment, sometimes normalised as a "rite of passage". Serious incidents must never be treated as mere disciplinary matters.
The Education Ministry's order for a comprehensive review, with instructions "not to hide anything", is therefore welcome.
But investigations after tragedies are not enough. What is needed is a systematic review of how schools identify risks, respond to complaints and protect students before violence occurs.
School safety measures and safeguards must therefore be thoroughly reviewed.
While each tragedy is different, repeated incidents should compel authorities to strengthen prevention, supervision and emergency responses.
This should include safety audits of schools, checks on CCTV coverage and blind spots, stronger access controls, attendance monitoring and closer supervision of students.
The education minister's latest directive must be translated into concrete action. Risks within schools and hostels must be identified early, with clear channels for students to report bullying, suspicious behaviour and threats before they escalate.
Schools must remain places of learning and safety, not places where violence is allowed to become normal.

Title: 14 companies approved to rehabilitate 7,500ha of abandoned rubber estates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Rubber Board has approved the participation of 14 estate management companies (EMCs) under the Consolidation Programme for Abandoned and Untapped Mature Rubber Areas as of September.
The Plantation and Commodities Ministry said this involved 7,576ha of abandoned rubber estates.
"Eight EMCs involving 3,719.47ha of identified abandoned areas have begun phased rehabilitation works since July," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply.
The ministry was responding to a question from Zahari Kechik (PN-Jeli) on the implementation of the programme to increase rubber production in Malaysia.
It said the programme, which began in 2025 and is expected to be completed in 2027, covers estates owned by government agencies and their subsidiaries, private estates, including rubber forest plantations, as well as smallholder plots.
The programme targets the rehabilitation of 3,000ha of abandoned and untapped mature rubber areas by 2027, aimed at bringing the land back into production and increasing national rubber output.
"Once the areas are brought back for tapping, rubber production is expected to increase gradually towards an additional target of at least 4,500 metric tonnes of natural rubber a year.
"The programme is also expected to create employment opportunities for rural communities, particularly younger people, while providing opportunities for cooperatives and rubber entrepreneurs to participate as EMCs," it said.

Title: MCBA seizes 637 tonnes of cocoa beans worth RM11.9mil at Johor port
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) seized 637 tonnes of cocoa beans worth nearly RM11.9 million smuggled into the country in a container at Pasir Gudang Port, Johor, on Saturday.
The agency, in a statement, said the beans were detected during an inspection by its enforcement officers about 3.50pm.
It said the beans were in 9,100 gunny sacks and had been brought in from Uganda.
"The value of the beans is estimated at RM11,886,444.72. The goods were found to have been imported with incomplete documentation that aroused suspicion. As such, the entire consignment was seized for further investigation," he said.
MCBA said any act or attempt to declare conflicting information at the country's entry points is an offence under Section 13 of the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011.
Anyone found guilty under the section is liable to a fine of not more than RM50,000, a jail term of up to two years, or both.
Subsequent offences can lead to a fine of RM75,000, jail term of up to five years, or both.

Title: Dozens quarantined in Siberia after plague institute lab worker dies
Article:
MOSCOW: A laboratory worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has fallen ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people, and the head of Russia's health watchdog to fly to the Irkutsk region.
The death has sparked public health fears on social media, but the authorities said on Monday the situation was under control.
Plague is endemic to Siberia, location of the first known prehistoric human outbreak, as the bacterium that causes it, Yersinia pestis, is present among the small wild mammals in its vast wilderness and their fleas. It is rare for Russians to fall ill with plague, however, though cases in other parts of the world - notably Africa - occur every year.
Local media named the woman as Darya Shipilova, an employee at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East.
There were conflicting reports about how and where the laboratory worker, whose age was given as 28, had fallen ill, but the authorities said she had died of pneumonia of as-yet unestablished origin.
AUTHORITIES SAY NO NEW CASES REPORTED, ALL CONTACTS TRACED
Russia's health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, told state media the institute had not found evidence of any accidents involving the handling of pathogens after rumours spread on social media that the woman had dropped a test tube containing live bacteria.
Nevertheless, Anna Popova, the head of Rospotrebnadzor, flew to Siberia for an emergency meeting over the weekend.
An unspecified number of people who had been in contact with the dead woman were quarantined, parts of the hospital in the town of Shelekhov where she died were cordoned off, and an aluminium plant told its workers to wear masks.
Authorities urged people to remain calm and said there was no evidence that the woman's death was linked to her work.
Igor Kobzev, the governor of the Irkutsk region, said in a statement that she had died of "pneumonia of unknown aetiology", adding: "Importantly, over the past few days, no new cases of staff from the Anti-Plague Institute seeking medical attention have been identified."
He said the situation was under control and that all known contacts of the dead woman had been identified, examined and placed under medical supervision.
Plague comes in three forms affecting different parts of the body. Pneumonic plague, an infection of the lungs, prompts the patient to cough out infectious airborne droplets.
If identified quickly, it can be treated with antibiotics. But if left untreated, it can be fatal in one to six days.

Title: Father of girl, 3, killed in Gerik crash hadn't seen her in a year
Article:
KOTA BARU: Mohamad Sanuzi Mohd Nawi had not seen his daughter in a year after divorcing her mother.
Then came the sad news that the 3-year-old was one of four killed in a three-vehicle road crash on the East-West Highway yesterday.
Safiyya Haura was killed along with her mother, Tuan Shazrin Tuan Mud, 40, and two other people in
a crash at Km38.5 of the highway
near Tasik Banding, Gerik, Perak, yesterday afternoon.
Sanuzi, 33, said he received a phone call from Taiping Hospital at 8pm on the day of the incident, informing him that his daughter and former wife had died.
"I was numb and unable to think of anything when I received the news, because (until then) I had been eagerly waiting for the moment I would meet Safiyya after a year of not seeing her, as she was in the care of my former wife, who lived in Perak.
"My wait ended with sad news, and it is even more painful because I can still hear Safiyya's voice, as she had just learnt to say 'papa' each time we made a video call.
"My ex-wife had told me she wanted to move back to Kelantan and planned to send Safiyya and her stepson, Mohammad Shiraz Hammani Abdul Fattah, 9, to my house in a few days," he said when met at Masjid Umari, Mukim Telaga Bata, Sering, here.
Besides the mother and daughter, the other victims were Al Zubir Deraman, 31, and Mohamad Hafiz Daniel Nik Hairey, 19.
Shiraz is in critical condition and is still being treated at Taiping Hospital.
The bodies of Tuan Shazrin and Safiyya were buried at the Kubur Dusun Muslim cemetery in Sering after isyak prayers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police to submit MCBA DG investigation paper to A-G tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The investigation papers on the incident involving Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will be handed over to the Attorney-General's Chambers tomorrow.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the investigation papers would be referred for further review, advice and instructions, in accordance with Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution.
"So far, statements have been recorded from 25 witnesses, comprising police officers and personnel, MCBA officers, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) auxiliary policemen, baggage handling system workers, medical officers and independent witnesses," he said in a statement.
Khalid said investigations began when two policemen lodged reports claiming they were physically manhandled by Shuhaily at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Sept 28.
He said federal police Criminal Investigation Department investigators launched a probe under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt.
"The investigation was conducted transparently, professionally and impartially, based on witness statements and evidence obtained to ensure every aspect of the incident is thoroughly examined.
"A conviction under Section 323 of the Penal Code carries a maximum prison sentence of a year, or a fine of up to RM2,000, or both," he said.
Khalid said people should not speculate on the incident, nor should they draw any conclusions, as these could jeopardise the investigation.
Previously, a video showing Shuhaily during an incident at KLIA Terminal 1 went viral on social media following an MCBA operation with a Aviation Security (AvSec) team against the activities of foreign touts at the airport.
Shuhaily later explained that a foreigner had been taken to the AvSec baggage inspection room before two individuals entered the area and recorded the incident.
He left it to the police to conduct further investigations into the incident and said he was prepared to accept any decision made by the government regarding the matter.
In a press conference at federal police headquarters in Bukit Aman earlier today,
Khalid had said police had recorded statements
from 25 people and obtained CCTV footage of the incident.

Title: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah visits Tun M at IJN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah visited former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad at the National Heart Institute (IJN) here yesterday.
The visit was shared on Dr Mahathir's official Facebook page, which said the Brunei ruler had visited the 101-year-old former prime minister at IJN on Oct 4.
Dr Mahathir was
admitted to IJN
on Sept 29 for observation, a day after his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, died at the same hospital at the age of 100.
On Oct 1, his son, Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, shared an update on his father's condition, saying it was better for Dr Mahathir to remain at IJN for now as being at home would remind him of Dr Siti Hasmah.

Title: Ministry takes RON95 samples from 11 petrols stations over water-mixing claims
Article:
ALOR SETAR: The Kedah Ministry of Domestic Trade and Costs of Living has taken RON95 petrol samples from 11 petrol stations in several districts for analysis following recent viral claims that the fuel was mixed with water.
State director Muhammad Nizam Jamaludin said the action followed public complaints that vehicles had broken down after refuelling at the affected stations.
"Ministry enforcement teams conducted inspections at 11 petrol stations today and took fuel samples from the involved tanks or pumps for inspection and further analysis.
"At the same time, preliminary inspections using the manual dipping method and a review of the Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) system readings showed no indication of the presence of water in the inspected fuel storage tanks," he said in a statement today.
He said the inspections covered Petron and Caltex stations in Alor Setar, Kubang Pasu, Sungai Petani and Kulim, as well as checks of fuel supply receipts, sales records and other relevant documents.
However, Muhammad Nizam said the preliminary findings were not conclusive, adding that the samples would be sent to the Department of Chemistry for analysis while the operators would also send samples to their respective oil companies' laboratories.
"The ministry will scrutinise the analysis results and the overall investigation findings before determining the next course of action, including taking appropriate measures if there is any violation of legal provisions," he said.
Members of the public can channel complaints via WhatsApp at 019-848 8000, the KPDN e-Aduan portal, the KPDN Call Centre at 1-800-886-800 or the KPDN EzADU smartphone application.

Title: Zetrix AI offers plan to settle RM314mil RTD arrears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has submitted a proposal to the government to resolve outstanding remittances following the suspension of its Road Transport Department (RTD) services from today.
In its statement today, Zetrix AI said its immediate priority is to resolve the outstanding obligations and work towards restoring the affected services, subject to necessary government approvals.
"Zetrix AI has submitted a proposed solution to the government of Malaysia to address the outstanding remittances for its consideration," it said.
The company did not disclose details of the proposal or the amount involved.
The move comes as the company faces RM314 million in outstanding government revenue collections, with Transport Minister Anthony Loke clarifying today that the amount relates to collections made between May 19 and Sept 30 this year.
Loke said the arrears were not accumulated over three years, as reported earlier, but had built up over several months.
The ministry and RTD reportedly had issued 35 reminders and held four engagement sessions with the company and other stakeholders to recover the money.
The issue came to wider attention last week when reports said Zetrix, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, owed the government more than RM200 million in unremitted collections.
The Straits Times, citing official documents and a government source, reported on Oct 2 that the amount had exceeded RM200 million by end-September and involved collections from road tax renewals, driving licences and traffic summonses.
However, Loke's latest clarification puts the outstanding amount at RM314 million and said the arrears covered the period from May 19 to Sept 30.
Loke also reportedly said the company submitted a post-dated cheque for RM231 million dated Sept 30, but the bank did not process the payment following instructions from the company.
The government subsequently suspended RTD payment services through MyEG and Zetrix AI effective Oct 5.
Zetrix AI, through the MyEG business, has been an RTD collection agent since 2000, handling services including motor vehicle licence renewals, vehicle ownership transfers, driving licence services and electronic summons payments.
Collection agents must remit government revenue within one working day of each transaction.
Zetrix AI said it regretted the inconvenience caused to customers and assured those who accessed affected RTD services before the suspension that their transactions had been processed and fulfilled.
It said further updates would be provided once information was confirmed.

Title: AG's Report: Govt accounts receivable down 1.1 per cent to RM102bil in 2025
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Government's Accounts Receivable (AR) fell by 1.1 per cent to RM102.032 billion in 2025 from RM103.158 billion the previous year, according to the Auditor General's Report 2/2026.
The report stated that the RM1.126 billion decrease was partly due to the write-off of revenue AR and loan interests amounting to RM1.207 billion, as well as RM603 million in guarantee fees no longer reported as AR.
Of the total, RM50.845 billion comprised Claimable Loans and Advances, while RM51.187 billion was Miscellaneous AR, down by 1.3 per cent and 0.9 per cent respectively, compared to 2024.
The report noted that non-compliance with the repayment schedule for Claimable Loans resulted in RM8.084 billion in arrears and RM578.32 million being written off.
The report also confirmed that total outstanding AR for utility relocation costs amounted to RM90.50 million. This amount includes RM30.46 million borne by the government, which should not have been recorded as outstanding AR.
The report recommended that the Federal Government strengthen its revenue collection mechanism through more strategic and effective measures.
This, it said, would help fund development expenditure more sustainably, reduce the fiscal deficit and decrease reliance on new borrowings.
It also suggested that the government take more proactive enforcement and monitoring actions to accelerate AR collection, reduce arrears and minimise the need for write-offs.

Title: Universities are not only path to youth success - Zambry Abd Kadir
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public need to change the perception that universities are the only avenue for developing talent and determining the success of young people, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said knowledge and skills in technical fields also opened up career opportunities for young people, including those who were less academically inclined.
"Over the past two years, we have often told the people that universities are not the only place for them to pursue their studies, but we also have other skills institutions such as polytechnics and community colleges that offer skills certificates in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
"For years, society has viewed polytechnics as a second choice for those who cannot get into university, but now applications to enter polytechnics have reached 132 per cent compared with 60 to 70 per cent previously," he said.
He said this during the "Technology Driving Change: Is Malaysian Talent Ready?" dialogue session held in conjunction with the launch of the Future Skills Framework for the Communications Sector and the Strategic Talent Development Initiative at Angkasapuri today.
Zambry said teaching approaches at skills institutions were also being strengthened to meet the country's demand for technical workers, including the government's effort to produce 60,000 engineers.
He said technical and engineering fields did not necessarily depend solely on degree qualifications, but also required skilled workers who had undergone engineering-related training at skills institutions.
Students from the arts stream with an interest and potential in the field were also being given opportunities to pursue it through suitable intervention programmes, he said, adding that polytechnics had so far trained 447 students through engineering diploma programmes.
Meanwhile, Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the skills mismatch issue needed attention, with nearly 37 per cent of skilled workers recorded as not working in the second quarter of this year, while the country's workforce stood at 16.8 million.
He said the situation was attributed, among other factors, to a lack of job opportunities, skills mismatches and less attractive salary offers in certain fields, making it necessary to strengthen the "future-proof talent" approach to ensure workers' skills were aligned earlier with future job requirements.
In efforts to strengthen workforce development, he said the Ministry of Human Resources had introduced the National Human Resources Policy 2026-2035, focusing on four aspects - more productive employment, career development, more meaningful incomes and appropriate protection.
However, Khairul Firdaus said the effectiveness of the policy needed to be supported by more balanced infrastructure development between states to ensure job opportunities and talent development were not concentrated only in the Klang Valley.

Title: Yemeni government forces seize district by Bab el-Mandeb, military sources say
Article:
RIYADH: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces seized key positions on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Monday, military and government sources said, as they fought to reverse last month's advances by the Iran-backed Houthis and drive them from the vital waterway.
The government forces have taken large parts of Dhubab district, which overlooks Bab el-Mandeb, and are asserting full control over the area with heavy air support from a Saudi-led coalition, three military sources and one government source told Reuters.
Houthi-aligned media had earlier denied that government forces had made advances in the area.
Fighting has raged along several frontlines in Yemen for weeks after a dormant civil war erupted in a spillover from the US-Iran conflict, with the Houthis seeking to control the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait and firing missiles and drones at Saudi cities and infrastructure.
With Gulf energy exports already restricted by Iran's closure of the Hormuz Strait, the fighting in Yemen has threatened another major oil export route, pushing up global prices and raising new risks in a region already aflame.
The internationally recognised Yemeni government announced on Sunday the launch of its offensive to recapture territory, with President Rashad al-Alimi swearing to fight "until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia."
Saudi Arabia backs offensive to retake territory
Saudi Arabia, which arms and trains Yemeni government forces, is backing the military campaign with air power and has sought logistical help from allies to push back the Houthis, restore free traffic in the Red Sea, and end the group's attacks on its territory.
While the war has raged on several frontlines in Yemen, the heaviest fighting has been in the southwest, both in the coastal area near the strait and in the hills around the city of Taiz, where the Houthis are trying to surround government forces.
A Houthi-run news agency on Monday cited a military source as saying that the group had driven government forces from the al-Mawasit district of Taiz province, reaching the home of Alimi, head of Yemen's interim presidential council.
The mountainous district sits close to the main road running from Taiz to Aden, the last route that government forces have had into the city, which has been on the frontlines since early in the civil war.
Yemen's conflict began after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in the following year with an air campaign aimed at restoring the government and ousting the Iran-backed group.
The fighting quickly ground to a bloody stalemate, with most frontlines stalled, leading to a major humanitarian crisis in what was already the poorest Arab state, until a ceasefire was agreed in 2022 that held until this summer.

Title: Four issues Felda must resolve under new plan
Article:
Zuraimi Abdullah
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Land Development Authority's (Felda) new strategic plan must address or redefine four fundamental issues if the agency is to achieve long-term financial sustainability.
They are Felda's commercial mandate, fragmented settler land, non-core assets and legal framework.
It is learnt that these were proposed by a special committee when it submitted Felda's new strategic direction to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Sept 25 this year.
The plan comes against the backdrop of the deep financial problems laid bare in Felda's 2019 White Paper, which included a forensic examination of eight investments and asset transactions.
The White Paper found that Felda's liabilities surged 1,100 per cent from RM1.2 billion in 2007 to RM14.4 billion in 2017, while its profit fell sharply.
By 2018, its cash reserves had dwindled to about RM35 million from RM2.5 billion between 2007 and 2011.
The forensic review also identified RM2.2 billion in impairment or losses across eight transactions, equivalent to about half the original investment value.
Among the transactions scrutinised was the RM2.3 billion acquisition of a 37 per cent stake in Indonesia's PT Eagle High Plantations, which was valued at only about RM500 million by March 2019.
The White Paper concluded that weak financial management and governance shortcomings had adversely affected Felda's financial position.
It called for restructuring its investment and loan portfolios and stronger governance and spending controls.
It is understood that the first issue is the need to draw a clearer line between Felda's commercial responsibilities and its wider social and political obligations.
The committee believed Felda cannot achieve financial independence if commercial decisions are continually driven by political considerations.
The belief is that if the commercial decision that determines its financial sustainability is always driven by political decisions, then Felda will never achieve financial sustainability and independence.
The new plan therefore needs to redefine Felda's mandate and determine which responsibilities should remain with the agency and which should be taken over by other government bodies.
For example, housing, education, healthcare and rural development should not automatically be funded by Felda if those responsibilities fall within the mandates of other agencies.
The second issue is the fragmentation of settler land through individual titles, inheritance and subdivision among successive generations.
The fragmentation makes it increasingly difficult to manage plantations as economically viable estates, affecting planting, harvesting, procurement and replanting.
A potential long-term leasing or professional management model could allow settlers to retain ownership while their land is managed collectively to preserve economies of scale.
However, any such model would have to clearly separate ownership, management and income distribution, with safeguards for settlers.
The third issue is Felda's portfolio of non-core investments and assets, including matters highlighted in the 2019 White Paper.
The plan needs to establish which assets can be recovered, restructured or should be recognised as effectively unrecoverable, rather than continuing to carry loss-making or non-strategic investments.
The Indonesian Eagle High investment is one example where Felda needs to determine whether further recovery efforts are commercially justified.
Some properties acquired during FGV's expansion after its 2012 listing could also be difficult to monetise because of falling values or unresolved legal, financial and governance issues.
The fourth issue is the legal framework governing Felda and its land.
It is learnt that three laws may need review or amendment of the the Group Settlement Areas Act 1960, the Land Development Ordinance of 1956 (or Felda Act), and the National Land Code 1965.
The laws need to address fragmented ownership, succession, land transfers and coordinated plantation management while protecting settlers' ownership rights.
The Felda Act may also need to clarify the agency's commercial mandate and its ability to undertake long-term leasing, professional management and restructuring arrangements.
Taken together, these four issues will determine whether Felda's new strategic direction can move the agency towards a more commercially sustainable model while preserving its core responsibility to settlers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersatu ready to discuss cooperation for Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is ready to discuss and refine the form of cooperation or an electoral pact for the upcoming Melaka state election, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali.
He said the matter was among the decisions reached at the Bersatu Political Bureau meeting chaired by its president, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, today.
Mohamed Azmin said the decision was made after taking into account views and analyses on Bersatu's participation in the Melaka election, including various aspects of the current political landscape.
He said Bersatu had also confirmed that it would use its own party symbol in the election, while the seats it would contest would be finalised soon.
"The decision to establish an electoral pact for the Melaka state election is aimed at optimising our potential to ensure the stability and continuity of a moderate and progressive state administration for the well-being of the people of Melaka.
"Bersatu appeals to the people of Melaka to give its candidates an opportunity to represent their voices, bring meaningful change and deliver direct benefits to all Melaka residents," he said in a statement today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 6m-tall tree falls across road in Batu Ferringhi
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 6m-tall tree fell across a road in Batu Ferringhi, but no injuries or vehicle damages were reported.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call at 4.27pm regarding the incident in front of the Spice Garden along Jalan Teluk Bahang.
"Firefighters from the Teluk Bahang station found a tree had fallen across the road when they arrived," he said.
John said three firefighters carried out cutting and clearing works to remove the obstruction.
"The operation was also assisted by the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Civil Defence Force," he said.
John said the situation was brought under control at 5.22pm, with the operation fully completed at 5.38pm.

Title: Johor to aid MoE in strengthening school security measures after Yong Peng murder
Article:
BATU PAHAT: The Johor government is ready to review and assist with basic infrastructure needs in schools across the state to strengthen security measures, says Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
He said this is to prevent a recurrence of the incident that led to the death of 16-year-old Form Four student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal at a secondary school in Yong Peng.
Onn Hafiz voiced full support for any initiative implemented by the Education Ministry, particularly the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in strategic areas within the school grounds.
"We have received a report on the incident and will look into every angle and opportunity to ensure student safety is better guaranteed," he said, adding that he would liaise with the ministry regarding student safety issues.
Speaking to reporters after visiting the victim's family in Kampung Parit Selamat today, he expressed deep sorrow on behalf of the state government, while urging the public to give police space to conduct a thorough investigation and refrain from speculation.
Meanwhile, State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said discussions would be held soon between the state education department and the Batu Pahat district education office.
He said the meeting would re-examine safety standard operating procedures (SOPs) in detail to address any existing weaknesses or shortcomings.
"This is not a matter to be taken lightly as it involves the loss of a life," he said.
On Saturday,
Irene Sofiya was found unconscious and bleeding
in the school hall at  5.50pm.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the victim sustained injuries to her head and body and was pronounced dead at the scene.
A post-mortem examination later confirmed that
she died of blunt force trauma
to the head.
Police detained her schoolmate,
a 16-year-old boy,
about 7pm the same day.
He was later remanded in custody for six days until Oct 9 to assist in investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Go Hub unit bags RM64.79 mil deal in maintenance, support services for KTMB ticketing system
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Go Hub Capital Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary NSS IT Solution Sdn Bhd has accepted a letter of acceptance from Tenang Capital Bhd (TCB) for the provision of maintenance and support services for the Integrated Ticketing System of Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) worth RM64.79 million.
TCB is a wholly owned subsidiary of KTMB.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the contract is for five years commencing from Oct 1, 2026 and expiring on Sept 30, 2031.
The contract is expected to contribute positively to the earnings and net assets of the company and its subsidiaries throughout the contract period, it added.

Title: Privasia Unit gets Miti nod for Bagan Datuk data centre project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Privasia Technology Bhd's indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, Silver Streams Technofarm Sdn Bhd (SSTF), has received approval from the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) to develop a data centre project in Bagan Datuk, Perak.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Privasia said MITI, via its letter dated Sept 7, 2026, approved SSTF's application for the development of the project.
"The approval granted by MITI is subject to standard regulatory terms and conditions, which include the requirement to secure an off-grid energy supply with a maximum demand of 50 megawatts.
"This must be in compliance with applicable guidelines, policies and renewable energy frameworks set by the Energy Commission and relevant authorities," it said.
It added that the project is specifically designed to meet this mandate through robust technical planning and structured energy sourcing to deliver an off-grid energy ecosystem that satisfies all regulatory and environmental benchmarks.
Privasia noted that SSTF has acknowledged and accepted the terms and conditions ahead of the Oct 6, 2026, deadline set by MITI, confirming its capability to fulfil all regulatory conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Citaglobal engineering unit secures RM29mil Thailand WTE supply contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd's subsidiary LAWI Engineering GmbH (LAWI Germany) has secured an engineering and equipment supply contract worth approximately RM29 million for the Siam Power Naklang waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Thailand.
Citaglobal said the contract covers the engineering, procurement and construction of the project's steam boiler plant, as well as basic engineering for the technology component of the overall WTE power plant.
LAWI Germany will undertake the imported engineering and equipment supply scope valued at approximately RM29 million, or EUR6.33 million, while its consortium partner will undertake the local scope valued at approximately RM23.1 million, or THB189.6 million.
The contract values exclude applicable taxes and duties, said Citaglobal.
Citaglobal Environment Management chief executive officer Thye Chee How said the contract builds on LAWI Germany's established track record in Thailand, where its technology is already operating in power plants.
"For Citaglobal, our investment in LAWI gives us a stake in a technology business with an established regional track record.
"Its proprietary systems and engineering expertise provide a strong platform for our Environment business to pursue further opportunities across Southeast Asia," said Thye.
The contract also builds on LAWI Germany's previous projects in Thailand, including the supply of waste-to-energy boiler systems for projects in Ayutthaya and Saraburi.
Since its establishment in 1996, LAWI Germany has completed more than 50 biomass and waste-to-energy power plant projects, with the majority located in Thailand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tech advances, including AI, gig economy, need workforce planning and regulation - Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid technological advancements such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), the gig economy, and e-commerce must be balanced with well-managed workforce planning and regulation to prevent social problems and negative implications for the local job market.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that if technological developments are allowed to run too freely without any regulation, it risks affecting workers' welfare and damaging the existing business ecosystem.
"On the government's part, we want to encourage it, but it comes at a price. Meaning if it is too free without regulation, there will be consequences. If too many citizens lose their jobs or do not get fair wages, that is why there is pressure.
"So I see there must be a balance between allowing companies and businesses to do some 'creative destruction', but not to the extent of causing damage and social problems, and not to the point of disrupting public order," he said.
He said this when serving as a panelist for the Dialogue Session 'Technology Driving Change: Is Malaysian Talent Ready?' in conjunction with the Launching of the Communications and Multimedia Future Skills Framework (C&M FSF) and Strategic Talent Development Initiative at Angkasapuri here today.
Also present as dialogue panelists were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and Deputy Minister of Human Resources Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akhbar Khan.
Meanwhile, when met after the event, Fahmi gave assurances to university students, university graduates, and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions that the emergence of new technologies also leads to the creation of new employment fields.
"In the sectors under the care of the Ministry of Communications, there are several things that companies need to take into account, including bachelor's degree graduates, university leavers, and those who may come from TVET fields.
"On the government's part, we will strive to ensure the available number of jobs allows these companies to hire more people, especially youths," he said.
Meanwhile, in a joint media statement with the Ministry of Communications, the Ministry of Higher Education (MoHE), and the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma), it was informed that the launch of the C&M FSF - spearheaded by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) - serves as a strategic reference for talent development in the sector for the next five to 10 years.
To ensure the implementation of this national reference framework achieve its targets, the Future Skills Talent Council (FSTC) has been established under the leadership of Kesuma in collaboration with MCMC, while MoHE acts to strengthen the curriculum and competencies of graduates in line with future industry needs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP: Police record statements from 25 witnesses in KLIA incident involving border agency chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Police have recorded statements from 25 witnesses as part of investigations into allegations that the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) physically assaulted two police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28.
In a statement issued today, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said that the two officers had lodged police reports over the alleged incident.
The case is being investigated by the Criminal Investigation Department at Bukit Aman under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which covers voluntarily causing hurt.
Those convicted under the provision face up to one year in prison, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
The 25 witnesses whose statements have been recorded include PDRM officers and personnel, AKPS officers, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) auxiliary police personnel, baggage-handling system workers, medical officers and independent witnesses.
PDRM said the investigation was being conducted transparently, professionally and impartially, based on witness statements and evidence gathered to ensure all aspects of the incident were examined thoroughly.
The investigation papers will be referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers on October 6 for consideration, advice and further directions, in accordance with Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution.
The public has also been advised against making speculation or drawing conclusions that could affect the ongoing investigation and legal process.

Title: Defence minister: LCS missile compensation claim expected to take time
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Recovering funds linked to the procurement of missiles for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) will not be resolved immediately and will take time, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
He said the delay is due to a lack of cooperation from the Norwegian government in resolving the issue.
He said that although requests for Norway’s assistance had been made at various levels, including by the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), Foreign Minister (Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan) and himself, Norway had refused to intervene.
“We do not see this matter being resolved quickly… even though Norway is the cause of the problem by refusing to grant the export licence.
“It (Norway) has done nothing to help us reach a decision that safeguards our rights and interests,” he said after the launch of the Siber Siaga 2026, held in conjunction with the Cyber Digital Services, Defence & Security Asia (CyberDSA) 2026 exhibition at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) here today.
Mohamed Khaled said the Norwegian government’s lack of intervention has left Malaysia to pursue its claim directly with the company, which he said has given various excuses.
“Recovering our money will not be easy. We expect it to be a lengthy process,” he said, stressing that efforts to complete the LCS weapon systems must continue regardless of the outcome of the claim against the supplier.
He said he would raise the matter with the government to discuss funding for new missiles, with the procurement involving several complex considerations, including the delivery timeframe.
The ministry must also ensure the new missiles can integrate with the LCS’s Combat Management System (CMS), which is nearing completion.
Malaysia reportedly has taken legal action against missile supplier Kongsberg Defense & Aerospace AS to seek compensation after the Norwegian government canceled the export license for Naval Strike Missiles (NSM) intended for the LCS project. — Bernama

Title: IGP: Don’t hide school safety issues to protect reputations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Safety issues in schools should not be concealed to protect reputations, as this may prevent authorities from taking action, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.
He said cooperation between the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and schools should be strengthened to ensure all incidents are reported for further action.
“Sometimes there are actions by certain parties attempting to hide issues to protect their reputation. But I believe if we enhance and strengthen this relationship, it can help resolve the problems,” he told a press conference after the launch of the PDRM Negotiator Handbook at the Bukit Aman Senior Officers' Mess here today.
Mohd Khalid said school safety is a shared responsibility requiring cooperation among PDRM, schools, the Ministry of Education, and parents. School liaison officers also regularly visit and coordinate with school authorities on safety issues.
He added that PDRM holds regular discussions with schools and parent-teacher associations on safety measures, including proposals to install closed-circuit television (CCTV). The Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department (JPJKK) has also increased patrols at schools and hostels.
On the death of a 16-year-old student at a school in Yong Peng, Johor, he said some details remain unconfirmed and the department will conduct a thorough investigation before making any conclusions.
Meanwhile, Mohd Khalid said PDRM has strengthened its Negotiator Cell, which was set up two years ago, by introducing a handbook for officers to use during crisis negotiations.
He said the cell, under the Internal Security and Public Order Department (KDNKA), has about 40 officers from various departments. The officers are selected based on their experience and can be deployed if a crisis requires negotiation expertise.
"If a crisis such as a kidnapping occurs, requiring advice, views, or negotiation between relevant parties, we will call upon the officers concerned to carry out the negotiation," he said.
He said the Negotiator Cell also works with other PDRM divisions as needed. The unit has also given lectures and shared experience in crisis management with the Royal Brunei Police Force.
Bukit Aman KDNKA deputy director (Crisis and Disaster) and Negotiator Cell commandant Datuk M.V Srikumar Nair said no standard response time is set for each case, as the duration depends on the circumstances and uniqueness of an incident.
"Every case is unique. Some information is received quickly, while other cases take time. Therefore, there is no standard response time," he said. — Bernama
